::: {#exm-plateau}
#### A cost with no stationary point

```{r}
#| label: plateau-sizes-r
#| echo: false
plateau_size_zero_pe <- 1 / (1 + exp(0))
plateau_size_ten_pe <- 1 / (1 + exp(10))
plateau_size_ten_sig_pe <- signif(plateau_size_ten_pe, 3)
```

Let $f(x) = \log\paren{1 + \e{-x}}$.
Its [derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) is
$\deriv{x} f(x) = -1 / (1 + \e{x})$,
which is negative for every $x$,
so $f$ has no [stationary point](#def-stationary-point) at all.

At $x = 0$ the [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative)
has size $`{r} plateau_size_zero_pe`$.
At $x = 10$ it has size $`{r} plateau_size_ten_sig_pe`$,
which is small but not zero.
A step of [gradient descent](#def-gradient-descent)
is the gradient times the [step length](#def-gradient-descent),
so the [iterates](#def-iterate) keep moving to the right,
more and more slowly.
With tolerance $\epsilon = 10^{-4}$,
the region $x \ge 10$ is a plateau (@def-plateau).
A run that enters it has not converged;
it has only slowed down.

:::
